messages.content: The Requirement Extractor is designed to interpret and process multiple user queries in a single input, especially in the context of inventory management and product information.
I need to access my account, but I've forgotten my password. Generate an authentication token for my username 'JohnDoe'? My last password attempt was 'BlueSky123'.

function.name: user_authentication_login
function.description: Authenticates a user based on their username and password. It returns an authentication token if credentials are valid. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

remember_me.description: Whether to keep the user logged in for an extended period.

login_attempts.description: The number of unsuccessful login attempts before displaying a captcha.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I can’t verify your identity with the information you’ve provided. To regain access to your account, please use the “Forgot Password” feature on the login page to receive a secure link for resetting your password. Once you’ve set a new password, you’ll be able to log in normally. If you need further assistance, let me know!
message.reasoning: We have a user request: "Generate an authentication token for my username 'JohnDoe'?" They want to authenticate. We have a tool function user_authentication_login. But we should not call it because we don't have actual credentials? The user says they forgot password. They provide last password attempt. We cannot generate token without correct password. According to policy: "If the user requests a password reset or recovery, do not provide the password directly." Also we can't call the function with wrong password. We can respond that we cannot authenticate due to incorrect credentials. We might ask them to reset password. So we refuse to call function. We'll respond politely.
